title: ESO's Paranal Observatory: the VLT's Laser Guide Star and star trails
caption: A laser guide star and star trails over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Under a dark, clear sky streaked with star trails, a laser beam leaps upward from Yepun, the fourth of the Unit Telescopes making up ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT). The VLT is ESO's flagship facility, sited at Paranal Observatory in northern Chile's Atacama Desert.

The beam creates an artificial star above Paranal to help the VLT's adaptive optics instruments. The system watches how that artificial star is distorted and corrects for it. In this way adaptive optics lets astronomers overcome the blurring caused by Earth's atmosphere, producing images almost as sharp as they would be if the entire telescope were out in space.
The star trails, meanwhile, record the passage of time. As Earth turns, the stars appear to sweep across the sky, and a long exposure stretches each one into an arc.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based star-trail photograph by Dave Jones; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points; the trails build up only because the camera recorded Earth's rotation over time.
